content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.5) and underperform when sentiment is low (<0.3), especially in early forecast periods.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment was >0.7 in prior 3–5 days.
- Underestimate in low-sentiment periods with recent price consolidation; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment <0.2 and price has been flat for 5+ days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is <0.4.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; adjust downward by 3–8% if sentiment is rising >0.6.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior, forecast should be 2–5% lower than model output to account for delayed market reaction.
